'''Christopher Jargocki''' (born Krzysztof Piotr Leopold Jargocki, {{IPA|pol|jarˌˈgɔtski}}, April 29, 1944 in [[Warsaw]], [[Poland]]), also known by the pen name Christopher Jargodzki, is a Polish-born American physicist, author, and translator who is a professor emeritus of Physics at the [[University of Central Missouri]], as well as the Director of the Center for Cooperative Phenomena.<ref name="c4cp">{{cite web |url=http://www.c4cp.org/ |title=Home |website=c4cp.org}}</ref>  He held a previous academic appointment at Northeastern University in [[Boston]].

==Early life==
Jargocki was born and raised in [[Włochy]], now a western district of Warsaw, the son of Stefania (née Lesinska) and Zdzisław Jargocki. After the [[Warsaw Uprising]], his father was taken to [[Auschwitz concentration camp|Auschwitz]], and then to [[Buchenwald concentration camp|Buchenwald]] where he died. Christopher Jargocki was raised as a Roman Catholic. At the age of 13, as a voice actor, he did dubbing work for the Russian children's movie [[Old Khottabych]]<ref>{{cite web|title=dubbing.fora.pl|url=http://www.dubbing.fora.pl/1949-59,18/rok-1957,78.html|work=Dziadek Hassan|accessdate=24 September 2013}} (in Polish)</ref>  based on a socialist-realist book by [[Lazar Lagin]].

==Education==
In 1957 Jargocki, age 13, enrolled in [[Lyceum]] No. 32 in Włochy,<ref>{{cite web |title=Historia szkoły przy ul. Promienistej we Włochach |url=http://www.promienista.waw.pl/historia.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090529190618/http://www.promienista.waw.pl/historia.html |archive-date=2009-05-29 |accessdate=24 September 2013}} (in Polish)</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Borucki|first=Juliusz|title=Szkoła cnót i charakterów : 70 lat szkoły na Promienistej|year=2008|publisher=Nakładem LXXIII Liceum Ogólnokształcącego|isbn=978-83-927984-0-8|pages=102|url=http://mbc.cyfrowemazowsze.pl/dlibra/docmetadata?id=6771&from=publication}} (in Polish)</ref> choosing the humanities orientation. After obtaining his [[matura]] (high school degree) at age 17 in 1961, Jargocki passed competitive entrance exams and enrolled in the Department of Physics at the [[University of Warsaw]]. He continued his education at the [[University of California]], [[Los Angeles]], earning a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[physics]] in 1966.  He entered a doctoral program at the [[University of California, Irvine]], where he received his doctorate in elementary particle theory in 1981.

==Writing career==

From 1966 to 1975 Jargocki worked part-time as a translator of books and articles from Russian and other languages into English for the [[American Mathematical Society]] and SCITRAN.

In 1977 Jargocki replaced [[Isaac Asimov]] as the contributing editor to the Science Digest Quick Quiz, a feature of ''[[Science Digest]]'', a monthly American magazine published from 1937 through 1986.

His four books, the last two co-authored with Franklin Potter, deal primarily with paradoxes and misconceptions in physics and astronomy.

==Awards and honors==

In 1996 he won a $10,000 award in the worldwide science and religion course competition sponsored by the [[John Templeton Foundation]] for a course entitled, ''Science and Religion:  From Conflict to Dialogue''. The course has become a component of the core curriculum at the University of Central Missouri.

In 2002 the book ''Mad About Physics'' was selected by the New York Public Library as one of the best books of the year 2001 in the teen category.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nypl.org/collections/nypl-recommendations/lists/bta2002|title = Books for the Teen Age 2002}}</ref>

In 2014 Christopher Jargocki was named a Kosciuszko Foundation Distinguished Fellow.<ref>The Kosciuszko Foundation, "Eminent Scientists of Polish Origin and Ancestry," http://www.thekf.org/kf/programs/eminentscientists/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919091755/http://www.thekf.org/kf/programs/eminentscientists/ |date=2015-09-19 }} Retrieved 8 August 2016</ref>

In 2019 he received an Albert Nelson Marquis Lifetime Achievement Award.<ref name="marquiswhoswho.com">{{cite web |url=https://www.marquiswhoswho.com/ |title=Home |website=marquiswhoswho.com}}</ref>

He is listed in American Men and Women of Science.

He is a VIP Listee with Marquis Who's Who.<ref name="marquiswhoswho.com"/>

==Center for Cooperative Phenomena==
In 2006, Jargocki founded the Center for Cooperative Phenomena to promote the study of the emergent, and specifically, cooperative phenomena at all levels of complexity from the physical to social sciences.<ref name="c4cp" /> One of his major areas of interest is the subject of synchronicity.

==Encyclopedia of Conversational English==
Jargocki founded the website in November 2013.<ref>ESL Encyclopedia of Conversational English, http://www.esldialogues.com/moodle/ {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611010209/http://www.esldialogues.com/moodle/ |date=2015-06-11 }} Retrieved 11 August 2016</ref> From the welcome page: "We hope that the Encyclopedia of Conversational English will become a standard reference and/or text for students and teachers of English as a Second Language, both in the United States and around the world. In a sense, the Encyclopedia may be viewed as a time capsule describing the language and culture of the United States and Great Britain as they have existed in the last 15-20 years."

Currently, the project comprises two volumes, Communication and Education, containing more than 2600 webpages. Volumes dealing with Daily Life and Transportation are forthcoming.
